"GINGERS DO HAVE SOULS!!" THE INTERNET WAS NEVER THE SAME AFTER THIS RANT 😭😂

This legendary viral moment features Michael Kittrell, better known online as CopperCab, from his famous 2010 YouTube video titled "GINGERS DO HAVE SOULS!!" The emotional webcam rant was a response to the widespread jokes and bullying directed at redheads, inspired in part by a 2005 South Park episode in which Eric Cartman claims that people with red hair have no souls. Clearly frustrated by the constant jokes, Michael passionately defended himself and other redheads, delivering an unforgettable reaction that quickly spread across the internet. His intense expressions, emotional delivery, and repeated declaration became instantly recognizable, turning an ordinary webcam video into one of the defining viral moments of early YouTube culture. 💀

What makes the story even more interesting is how quickly the video evolved beyond its original message. Internet users began creating remixes, parodies, reaction videos, and musical edits, including a famous version by the comedy music group schmoyoho. CopperCab became a recognizable internet personality, and the original rant eventually became a piece of early-2010s meme history. Although the internet mostly remembers the exaggerated reactions and hilarious remixes, the original video came from someone genuinely frustrated with being mocked for his appearance. More than a decade later, that unforgettable declaration still lives on as one of YouTube's most recognizable viral catchphrases. 😭🔥

Some games just mean more. 
Every time we showed up to play Georgia, i wanted to try to bring my best. 
For my family.
My teammates.
My coaches.
And my dad, whose belief in me made it all possible.
my senior year I had the the privilege of breaking Herschel Walker's touchdown record in Jacksonville against Georgia. Such an incredible athlete, one of I think one of the greatest players to have ever played in Herschel Walker. And then we called 96 Q Mickey, which is named after our strength coach Mickey Marati. And I remember jabbing outside, coming back inside and being able to run and score a touchdown and celebrate with the pouncies and everybody else. And all my teammates were telling me, you broke Herschel's record, like get the ball. And so I went to the ref and I was asking him for the ball and he was like, oh no no, and the pouncies are you know, like, yeah, give him the ball. And so I finally got the ball and I got to give that ball to my dad for Christmas. And uh it was one of my favorite gifts I've ever given him. Um to just say what he meant to me and the only reason I had the chance of of breaking that was because the belief and love he had for me. Um Still miss, Dad. Yeah. Um but giving him that ball, what it represents was his support, him believing in me, him supporting me so I could play this awesome game.

source_items.body:
"GINGERS DO HAVE SOULS!!" THE INTERNET WAS NEVER THE SAME AFTER THIS RANT 😭😂

This legendary viral moment features Michael Kittrell, better known online as CopperCab, from his famous 2010 YouTube video titled "GINGERS DO HAVE SOULS!!" The emotional webcam rant was a response to the widespread jokes and bullying directed at redheads, inspired in part by a 2005 South Park episode in which Eric Cartman claims that people with red hair have no souls. Clearly frustrated by the constant jokes, Michael passionately defended himself and other redheads, delivering an unforgettable reaction that quickly spread across the internet. His intense expressions, emotional delivery, and repeated declaration became instantly recognizable, turning an ordinary webcam video into one of the defining viral moments of early YouTube culture. 💀

What makes the story even more interesting is how quickly the video evolved beyond its original message. Internet users began creating remixes, parodies, reaction videos, and musical edits, including a famous version by the comedy music group schmoyoho. CopperCab became a recognizable internet personality, and the original rant eventually became a piece of early-2010s meme history. Although the internet mostly remembers the exaggerated reactions and hilarious remixes, the original video came from someone genuinely frustrated with being mocked for his appearance. More than a decade later, that unforgettable declaration still lives on as one of YouTube's most recognizable viral catchphrases. 😭🔥
